The evacuation of United Nations troops and North Korean civilians by sea from the port of Hungnam, on the northeast coast of Korea, from 15 to 24 December 1950, during the Korean War.

In late 1950 UN forces had pushed deep into North Korea. Then Chinese armies entered the war and drove them back. American and South Korean troops, after the hard fight at the Chosin Reservoir, fell back on Hungnam. The UN command decided to take them out by sea, with their equipment.

Tens of thousands of North Korean civilians crowded the docks, hoping to escape. Ships took about 100,000 of them along with about 100,000 troops. The cargo ship SS Meredith Victory, built for a few dozen people, carried some 14,000 refugees to Geoje Island, and no one died on the way. Five babies were born on board.

The port was blown up as the last ships left. Many families were split forever by the new border. Among the refugees were the parents of Moon Jae-in, later president of South Korea.
sum: The evacuation of United Nations troops and North Korean civilians by sea from the port of Hungnam, on the northeast coast of Korea, from 15 to 24 December 1950, during the Korean War.
